label: copy phase: input j, about to output m, late in the copy
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never in the original or delimiter phases), almost always when the fed-back input is j (94% of mass; m input covers the remaining 6%), and never before recall_idx 3. Its strongest preference is for the j -> m transition: input j while output m (72% of mass). The top examples are all ...j m <DEL> ... [j]. Activation rises with absolute step t and with L. The rate climbs from 0.3x lift at t=8 to 12x at t=17, and the largest activations occur at t=16-17 in L=9 sequences. Weaker firing occurs on input j followed by output j, i, h and other tokens, and these are missed by the predicate. Does not fire on j when it appears early in the copy (recall_idx < 3), on first occurrences of any token, or on tokens other than j and m. Precision is limited because many late j->m steps stay inactive, especially at smaller t.
